questions.q: How did Rikki-tikki end up lying on the garden path of the bungalow?
choices: A hawk dropped him there after catching him in the fields
A summer flood washed him out of his burrow and down a ditch
Teddy found him in the long grass and carried him home
He ran away from his family to look for a house to live in
questions.evidence: a high summer flood washed him out of the burrow

questions.q: When Rikki-tikki woke on the path he was "very draggled indeed." What does "draggled" mean here?
choices: Wet, dirty and messy
Hungry and thin
Angry and ready to fight
Badly hurt and bleeding

questions.q: Why is it so hard to frighten a mongoose, according to the story?
choices: He has thick fur that no teeth can get through
He is eaten up with curiosity from nose to tail
His mother teaches him never to show any fear
He is much stronger than he looks to other animals
questions.evidence: he is eaten up from nose to tail with curiosity

questions.q: What happened when Rikki-tikki climbed into the big man's lap to see how writing was done?
choices: He knocked the pen and the papers onto the floor
He fell asleep there until the lamps were lit
He burned his nose on the end of the man's cigar
He bit the man's finger by mistake and was scolded
questions.evidence: burned it on the end of the big man's cigar

questions.q: Teddy's father says Teddy is "safer with that little beast than if he had a bloodhound." What does he believe?
choices: The mongoose will keep burglars away from the house at night
The mongoose will teach Teddy to be braver about the dark
The mongoose would protect Teddy if a snake came in
The mongoose is too small and gentle ever to bite a child
questions.evidence: If a snake came into the nursery now

questions.q: Why were Darzee and his wife crying in their nest?
choices: Nag had eaten one of their babies that fell out
A storm had torn the leaves of their nest apart
Rikki-tikki had frightened their babies away
Their eggs had been stolen by the musk-rat
questions.evidence: One of our babies fell out of the nest yesterday and Nag ate him.

questions.q: "Darzee and his wife only cowered down in the nest without answering." What does "cowered" mean?
choices: Sang softly to calm themselves
Crouched low in fear
Stood up tall to look brave
Flew away as fast as they could
questions.evidence: only cowered down in the nest without answering

questions.q: Why was the big cobra Nag secretly afraid of Rikki-tikki?
choices: Rikki-tikki was much bigger than any mongoose he had seen
He knew a grown mongoose's business is to fight and eat snakes
The big man had told him the mongoose belonged to the house
Darzee had warned him that the mongoose had killed his brother
questions.evidence: at the bottom of his cold heart, he was afraid

questions.q: While Nag was talking to Rikki-tikki, what was Nagaina doing?
choices: Hiding the eggs deep in the melon bed
Climbing the thorn-bush to reach Darzee's nest
Creeping up behind Rikki-tikki to strike him
Sliding into the bungalow through the bath sluice
questions.evidence: She had crept up behind him as he was talking

questions.q: After the cobras disappeared into the grass, why did Rikki-tikki not follow them?
choices: He heard Teddy calling him in for breakfast
He was not sure he could manage two snakes at once
He had been bitten and needed to rest for a while
Darzee begged him to stay and guard the nest
questions.evidence: he did not feel sure that he could manage two snakes at once

questions.q: According to the story, what really decides a fight between a mongoose and a snake?
choices: Which one is quicker with its eyes and its feet
A magic herb the mongoose eats after being bitten
Which animal is larger and heavier than the other
How long each one can go without food or water
questions.evidence: The victory is only a matter of quickness of eye and quickness of foot

questions.q: Why does Karait, the dusty brown snakeling, do so much harm to people?
choices: He hides in shoes and beds inside houses
He is so small that nobody thinks of him
He can climb walls and reach any window
He travels in large groups through gardens
questions.evidence: he is so small that nobody thinks of him

questions.q: Why did Rikki-tikki decide not to eat Karait after killing him?
choices: Snake meat made young mongooses sick
Teddy's father took the dead snake away at once
A full meal would make him slow, and he must stay quick
He was already full from his breakfast of banana and egg
questions.evidence: a full meal makes a slow mongoose

questions.q: "'Do you think a snake-killer kills muskrats?' said Rikki-tikki scornfully." How did Rikki-tikki say it?
choices: In a frightened, shaky whisper
As if the idea was silly and beneath him
In a kind voice, to comfort a friend
Very slowly, as if he were half asleep

questions.q: What is Chuchundra the musk-rat like?
choices: Timid and sad, always creeping by the wall
Brave and boastful, always picking fights
Sly and tricky, a secret friend of the cobras
Cheerful and noisy, the news-teller of the house
questions.evidence: Chuchundra is a broken-hearted little beast

questions.q: What faint sound did Rikki-tikki hear in the silent house at night?
choices: The tapping of a beak against the window glass
The dry scratch of snake scales on brick-work
Chua the rat gnawing at the kitchen door
Water dripping slowly from the big bath jar
questions.evidence: the dry scratch of a snake's scales on brick-work

questions.q: Why did Nagaina want the people in the bungalow killed?
choices: The big man had cut down the thorn-bush where she hunted
Teddy had thrown stones at her eggs in the garden
Then the mongoose would leave and the garden would be theirs
She wanted to live inside the cool bath-rooms all summer
questions.evidence: When the house is emptied of people

questions.q: What is this first part of the story mostly about?
choices: A mongoose who finds a new home and learns of its snake enemies
A family who moves to India and learns how to garden in the hot sun
A tailorbird who builds a nest that no snake in the garden can reach
A musk-rat who finally finds the courage to run across the room
